info.title: LumenBox client API
info.description:
LumenBox client API, v1 (docs/106 §4). Additions only inside v1: a new operation, a new optional field, a new known value — each raises the revision `GET /api/v1/meta` reports.

Conventions, the same for every operation:
- JSON, camelCase. Ids are opaque strings: compare them, never parse them. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC, to the second (`2026-11-28T10:00:00Z`).
- A field with no value is absent, never null.
- A client ignores fields it does not know.
- A string listed with `x-extensible-enum` is an open enumeration: a client treats a value it does not know as "other", shows the item's plain words, and offers to open it on the page or the desktop app when it cannot act on it.
- Lists take `?limit=` (1–100) and `?cursor=` and answer `{ items, nextCursor }`; `nextCursor` is absent on the last page.
- Errors are `{ code, error, requestId }`: `code` is stable and is what a program reads; `error` is a sentence in the request's language (`Accept-Language`). Every answer carries `X-Request-Id`.
- An unknown path answers 404 `api-operation-unknown`; a known path with a method it does not take, 405 `api-method-not-allowed`. A resource the caller may not see answers 404 exactly as one that does not exist.
- Reads carry `ETag`; a request with a matching `If-None-Match` answers 304 with no body.
- Every `POST` accepts `Idempotency-Key`: a repeat within 24 hours with the same body answers the first answer.
- 429 carries `Retry-After` in seconds.
- A deprecated operation answers with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers for a full release line before it goes. Operations listed in `meta.preview` may change in any release.

Credentials (`Authorization: Bearer`): a personal token (`lbxp_…`) is a person's own script; a service token (`lbxs_…`) is an integration an Admin named, limited to its view.
What a call may do is the person's role, intersected with the token's scopes, intersected with what that person may see; a token never raises anything.
Cross-origin browser calls are not answered with CORS headers.

get.summary: What changed since a position, durably
get.description:
For a client waking from sleep, starting, or reconnecting: what changed since `since`, read from a ledger on the server's disk that survives restarts and is kept 30 days. A change is listed only when the caller may read the thing now (or, gone, could have read it); its words are fetched, not sent. Changes are of work and agents; an agent's `status` (working or idle) is not a change. Any credential: each change is shown by the scope its type needs — `work:read` for work, `agents:read` for agents — and a credential without that scope is not told of it.

Any credential.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: The `durableSeq` from the last answer; 0 the first time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many changes at most. 1 to 1000; 500 when absent.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: An `ETag` this client holds: 304 when it still matches.

200.description: What changed since `since`, oldest first, each thing once (its newest change). When `reset` is true the gap is older than what the server keeps (30 days), or `since` is from another installation's history: drop what is cached, read it again (`/work`, `/agents`, `/board`), then go on from `durableSeq`.

get.description:
`text/event-stream`, for a client in the foreground. Each `change` event's data is a `ChangeRecord` and its `id` is the record's `seq`. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` (what `EventSource` sends) and the stream first replays, from the same durable ledger as `/changes`, each thing changed since, once; then a `ready` event whose `id` is the newest position. When the gap is older than the ledger keeps, the first event is `reset` (data `{ "durableSeq": n }`): reload, then go on. With no `Last-Event-ID` the stream starts now. A `: ping` comment comes every 20 seconds. The stream ends when the credential stops being valid. What a credential may be told of is as for `/changes`.

Any credential.

parameters.description: The `id` of the last event this client read: the stream replays what changed since.

bearer.description:
A personal token (`lbxp_…`) or a service token (`lbxs_…`). Scopes:
- `agents:read`: Read the agents the person may reach.
- `work:read`: Read work, its history and the board.
- `work:decide`: Answer what waits on the person: count work as done, put it off, stop it, approve or deny.
- `chat:read`: Read conversations the person may read.
- `chat:write`: Send messages and card actions in conversations the person may drive.
- `files:read`: Read deliverables.
- `devices:manage`: List and remove the person's own devices.
- `desktop:view`: Watch an agent's desktop.
- `desktop:control`: Drive an agent's desktop.

Error.description: A refusal. A program reads `code`; `error` is a sentence for a person, in the request's language (`Accept-Language`).

code.description: Stable: what a program matches on. A code it does not know is handled by the HTTP status.

error.description: What happened and what to do, for a person. Never matched on: the words change.

requestId.description: Names this request in the server's log.

Meta.description: What this server is and can do. Read before signing in, and to see what the server answers instead of guessing from a version.

api.description: "1.<revision>": the revision rises with every addition to v1.

server.description: The LumenBox version of the server.

capabilities.description: Every stable operation this server answers.

preview.description: Operations this server answers that may change in any release (docs/106 §1).

mode.description: A personal installation (one Owner, the desktop app) or an organisation's server.

Me.description: The person the credential acts for, and the credential.

name.description: The person's name as the installation shows it.

role.description: What the person may do: `viewer` watches, `driver` instructs agents, `admin` runs the installation.

homeAgentId.description: The agent a direct message from this person reaches, when there is one the credential may read.

Credential.description: The credential this request was made with. Never the token.

id.description: The credential's id: what revoking it names.

kind.description: `personal`: a person's script. `service`: an integration an Admin named, reading through its view. `device`: a phone or desktop client.

label.description: The name it was given when it was minted.

scopes.description: What it may be used for.

lastUsedAt.description: When it was last used, to the minute; absent before its first use.

ServiceView.description: What a service token may read (present on service credentials only). Nothing is visible unless named here, and a view never reaches past what its Admin may see.

allAgents.description: Every agent the Admin may reach.

allWork.description: All work the readable agents hold.

workIds.description: This work and the work made for it, when `allWork` is false.

conversationText.description: Whether conversation text and work descriptions are included. False: titles, states and results only.

Agent.description: An agent the caller may reach: one in a box the person is a member of (and, for a service token, one its view names).

description.description: What the agent is for, as its profile says.

boxId.description: The box the agent works in.

items.description: A team: a label on agents in one box.

teams.description: The teams the agent is on.

isHome.description: Whether a direct message from the person reaches this agent.

AgentPage.description: A page of agents, by name.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor; absent on the last page.

Work.description: A piece of work, as the page's All work and board show it. Built from the task; never the task itself.

title.description: What it is, in a line.

state.description: The board's state: `open` — asked for, not started (a client's "ready"); `doing` — being worked on ("in progress"); `blocked` — waiting on something or somebody ("blocked"; when the person is that somebody, `waitsOnMe` is true); `review` — handed in, waiting for a reviewer ("in review"); `done` — accepted; `dropped` — given up, kept for the record. There is no "needs you" state: whether it waits on the person is `waitsOnMe`, which any state but `done` and `dropped` may have.

topLevelId.description: The top-level work this belongs to: its own id when nothing made it, else the id of the work at the top of what it was made for.

parentId.description: The work this was made for, when it was made for another.

agentId.description: The agent doing it, when one is and the caller may read that agent.

conversationId.description: The conversation it was asked in, when there is one.

waitsOnMe.description: Whether the person owes something on it now: an answer, a review, a decision. The same mark the page puts on its row.

summary.description: The newest thing said about what was done (the result so far), cut to 700 characters.

description.description: The request in full. Absent for a service token whose view does not include conversation text.

due.description: When it is due: a date (`2026-12-01`) or a time, as given.

WorkPage.description: A page of work, most recently changed first. Work that changes while a client pages moves to the front; `/changes` says so.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor; absent on the last page.

WorkChange.description: One change in a piece of work's history.

byKind.description: Who: a person, an agent, or the installation itself (a reminder, a check, a restart).

byId.description: Their id, for a person or an agent.

byName.description: Their name, for a person or an agent.

state.description: The state it moved to, when it moved.

agentId.description: The agent it was handed to, when this change handed it on.

note.description: What was said with it. Absent for a service token whose view does not include conversation text.

WorkChangePage.description: A page of a piece of work's history, oldest first.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor; absent on the last page.

Board.description: The board: the work the caller may read, as columns by state, each in the order the page shows — what waits on the person first, then the most recently changed.

columns.description: One per state, in board order: open, doing, blocked, review, done, dropped.

title.description: The column's name, in the request's language.

total.description: How much work is in the column; `cards` holds the first `limit` of it. The rest: `GET /work?state=`.

cards.description: The column's work, in board order.

ChangeRecord.description: That something a client may hold changed: never what it now says. Fetch it (`GET /work/{id}`, `GET /agents/{id}`); a 404 then means it is gone, or no longer the caller's to read, and the client drops it.

seq.description: Rises with every change, across restarts: the position to resume from.

op.description: `upsert`: it is new or changed. `delete`: it is gone.

Changes.description: What changed since `since`, oldest first, each thing once (its newest change). When `reset` is true the gap is older than what the server keeps (30 days), or `since` is from another installation's history: drop what is cached, read it again (`/work`, `/agents`, `/board`), then go on from `durableSeq`.

items.description: The changes the caller may be told of.

durableSeq.description: Send it as `since` next time: everything up to it has been looked at.

hasMore.description: Whether more changes follow `durableSeq` now: ask again at once.

reset.description: Whether the client must reload instead (see above).
